text:
cheng: FYI canary warmstart (mixed-quant AWQ+INT8 hybrid) is showing a big MLQA drop after yesterday's roll.
marta: how big? example?
cheng: EM went 87.3 -> 62.1 on mlqa-en (full eval). quick example: prompt/question -> model answer is confidently wrong and invents a source.
cheng: example output:
```
Q: Where did the 1998 conference take place?
GT: Paris
AWQ-hybrid: "It was held in the American Convention Center, Chicago, 1998. See: The Proceedings of the American Symposium."
```
cheng: that's hallucinated location + fake citation. Also seeing broken punctuation/JSON-like escapes in structured outputs (table cells dropped).
marta: ouch. is this only on mlqa or other suites?
eval-bot: eval-summary: model=awq-mix-warmstart-v1, suite=mlqa-en, size=10k, EM=62.1 (baseline gptq-fp16 EM=87.3), F1=70.4 -> 89.1 baseline, sample_failures=412
nate: can we confirm it's the quant path? please run gptq and fp8 baselines on the same canary payload.
cheng: plan: bisect candidate set: (1) awq-mix-warmstart-v1 (current), (2) awq-single-no-warmstart, (3) gptq-fp16, (4) fp8-quiet. running small quick-pass now.
taylor: also check tokenization — warmstart changed shared tokenizer flags earlier. tokenization mismatch can shift alignments and look like hallucination.
taylor: run token diff:
```
python infra/token_diff.py --model awq-mix-warmstart-v1 --text "Where did the 1998 conference take place?"
```
sam: can we rollback routing to gptq fallback for the canary? i can flip traffic to route->gptq-fallback for warmstart-canary-3.
marta: do that if it buys time. but we need root cause first.
cheng: quick log snippet from the canary run showing KV evictions around long contexts:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] kv_cache: shard=3 evict_count=8 window_size=2048
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] attention_kernel: fallback_path=quant-degraded
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] generate: sample=1234 tokens=128 seed=42
```
nate: curious if warmstart's shared-pool splitpack config changed batch boundaries. that can corrupt alignment when combined with AWQ packing.
taylor: re-run focused eval with seed=42 and deterministic sampling:
```
ri-eval run --suite mlqa-en --model awq-mix-warmstart-v1 --seed 42 --deterministic --limit 2000 --save failures.json
```
cheng: running that now. I'll upload failures.json when done.
eval-bot: job queued (id=ev-8923) ETA ~18m. will post top-20 failures when ready.
sre-bot: noticed a deploy at 2026-03-18T08:55:31Z -> commit=3a7b2f4 warmstart:enabled true
marta: commit hash? can ops share deploy diff (quant libs / kernel selectors)?
sre-bot: deploy diff link: https://deploys.internal/revisions/3a7b2f4
sam: rolling gptq fallback now to canary-3 :thumbsup:
cheng: quick manual comparison on 50 samples:
- gptq-fp16: 50/50 correct (sanity)
- awq-mix-warmstart-v1: 32/50 correct, 12 hallucinated, rest formatting hiccups
- awq-no-warmstart: 45/50 correct
conclusion: warmstart path + AWQ interaction likely trigger.
marta: actionable: 1) scale eval (done by cheng) 2) reproduce with identical tokenizer + seed 3) if repro, rollback warmstart flag for canary 4) open infra ticket to audit shared-pool splitpack change
nate: I'll run microbench to compare attention kernel select trace between awq and gptq. suspect kernel selector picks quant-degraded path incorrectly for mid-length sequences.
taylor: adding tokenization diff to checklist. also check byte-level spaces/newline handling.
cheng: created ticket ML-2938 with links to failures.json and diff logs. assigned to eng-ml. PR 5989 pinned warmstart toggle for canary configs.
sam: routing flipped, traffic now 0% to awq-mix-warmstart-v1 on warmstart-canary-3. monitoring.
marta: good. meeting 10:30 to triage results. thx all :eyes:
nate: ETA for microbench traces ~30m.
cheng: eval complete: failures.json uploaded -> top 3 failure clusters: hallucinated facts (36%), JSON escape corruption (28%), dropped table rows (22%). linking in ticket.
marta: nice work. schedule a canary rollback if failures don't clear in 1h. keep me posted.
cheng: will update ticket and paste a short reproducibility checklist after meeting.
